Methodology

Evidence over hype.

Our process is built around probability estimates, price comparison and careful team-news checks — not claims about "must-win" teams.

What we predict

Only the full-time 1X2 market: 1 = home team wins, X = draw, 2 = away team wins. We do not currently publish corners, cards, totals or accumulator tips.

What expected value (EV) means

EV = (model probability × decimal odds) − 1

For example, a probability of 60% at odds 1.80 yields EV of +8%. This is a theoretical expectation only if the probability estimate is correct. High EV estimates can be errors, especially when the model misses team news.

Our baseline screen

1

Find a plausible candidate

For a value candidate, estimate the complete 1/X/2 probabilities using only pre-match data. Compare our model with bookmaker consensus and check for draw risk. Do not apply a 70% ceiling when ranking the safest favourite.

2

Price the risk

For value picks, calculate theoretical EV and normally require at least +3%, but only after accounting for model calibration, lineups and market disagreement. A high win probability and a positive EV are two different criteria.

3

Verify the football reality

Check injuries, suspensions, probable lineups for both teams, rest, rotation, home advantage, tactical matchups and motivation. Unverified news is not treated as fact. Reject stale model probabilities.

4

Lock the prediction before kickoff

Record date, matchup, market, three outcome probabilities, odds, publish time, model version and data coverage. Later record the score and outcome without altering the original forecast.

Daily featured match versus value picks

Featured match: The matchup with the highest conservatively adjusted 1X2 win probability among today's fixtures, after checking data quality, injuries, rotation and the market consensus. It is displayed as a candidate with uncertainty — never a safe or guaranteed win. If coverage is inadequate, the page says no reliable featured match.

Value picks: A separate list. Matches appear only if an estimated edge remains after all checks. Some days this list is empty. We do not lower a probability threshold to produce a daily bet.

Model improvement and evaluation

Before a match, we log separate probabilities for home win, draw and away win (summing to 100%). The market probabilities (after removing bookmaker margin) serve as a benchmark, alongside an independently estimated model based on recent expected goals, team strength, home advantage, schedule and team news. We then evaluate calibration, Brier score and out-of-sample accuracy, not only profit or the win rate. The weights and thresholds remain provisional until validated on predictions recorded before kickoff.

How are borderline prices handled?

The standard price screen starts above 1.50. A borderline record just outside this range is disclosed as a separate observation, not counted as a strict-rule model pass. The analysis still needs to explain the football case and the uncertainty.

What these numbers do not mean

A model's 70% does not guarantee seven wins out of every ten picks. We need a large, prospective record to evaluate calibration and long-run performance. We never publish an ROI or win rate until actual settled records exist.
